# The Data Science Process 

##  A simplified way of thinking about the data science process: 

![Figure by Florian Huber, 2026](images/fig_asemic_data_science_workflow.png){fig-align="center"}

## Another condensed way of thinking about the data science process 

![](images/Condense_DSProcess.png){fig-align="center"}

## ASEMIC Data Science Process 

Captures the essence of a typical data science project. Crucially, while presented linearly, **real-world data science is an iterative, cyclical process** 

![Figure by Florian Huber, 2026](images/fig_asemic_data_science_workflow.png){fig-align="center"}

## Data Science Workflow {.smaller}

The data science process consists of a wide variety of **different phases or steps**, which ultimately also leads to the wide **variety of techniques and tools** that need to be used throughout such a process.

* different skills and expertise are required for different phases of a typical data science project

![Figure by Florian Huber, 2026](images/fig_asemic_workflow_example.png){fig-align="center"}

## Data Science is Science ⚖️ 🔍

::: {.incremental}
⚖️ You might be used to science looking like this:

* theory > hypothesis > data 
* This is **confirmatory analysis**, a **deductive** approach to knowledge 
* Asks: "Is this specific hypotheses supported by the data?"

:::

## Data Science is Science ⚖️ 🔍 {transition="none"}

When doing data science projects, we are often using data we did not collect where we do not have to context to be testing pre-defined hypothesis. 

What do we do? 

# Explore! 🔍

## Exploratory Data Analysis 🔍

Finds patterns and generates new hypotheses from data

::: {.incremental}
* data > patterns > theory
* This is an **inductive** approach to knowledge that generates hypotheses and leads to open-ended discovery
* Asks: "What does the data suggest?"

:::

## Successful exploratory analysis starts with **context**

* *not* data visualisation or narrative, these come later 
* in this course we are learning about and using *data storytelling* techniques

![Image by Brent Dykes](images/DataStorytelling.jpg){width=50%}

## Data storytelling: a brief introduction

Begin with the context around the need to communicate 

* understand the circumstances around each metric in a given data set 
* transition from data discovery (**exploratory analysis**) to data communication (**explanatory analysis**)

## After exploring the data, move to explanatory thinking {.smaller}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
* Exploration = observing patterns 
* Before finalising data visualisations & composing your narrative, you must consider 

  1. Who is your audience?
  2. Who do you need your audience to know or do? 
  3. How will you communicate to your audience?
  
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/DataStorytelling_Venn.jpg)
:::

## {#slide23-id data-menu-title="R Pros and Cons" footer="false"}

::: {.incremental}
::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### **Advantages**

* Open Source Software 
  - Free!!
* New methods implemented faster 
* More flexible/customizable 
* Anyone can contribute 
  - Do not have to work at R to contribute to R 
  
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .smaller}
### **Disadvantages**

* No centralised support
* Many find it harder to learn - but that is why we are here! 
* Less consistency across procedures - other software you rely on the programmers
* …Anyone can contribute (some packages are better than others)

:::
::::: 
:::

## Further (selected) reasons why R! {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
* High quality and robust data visualisation 
  - e.g., `{ggplot2}` — covered in depth in week 6 
* Go-to language for statistics and data science; used in almost every industry 
* Vast R community support 
  - Stack Overflow 
  - #Rstats on social media  
  - etc. 

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}
* The most comprehensive statistical analysis package, new technology & ideas open appear first in R 
* The `{tidyverse}` ecosystem
* You can do many things beyond data analysis/processing…maps, calendars, etc.! 
* It can be very satisfying and fun once you get the hang of it!

:::
::::: 
:::

## R Syntax 

There are 3 main types of syntax you might come across in R:

1. base R (`$`) 
2. tidyverse (`%>%`)
3. formula (`~`) 

![](images/syntax_columns.png){fig-align="center"}

# Bar chart demonstration in R using health care data 

# Top Tips in starting your R journey 

## 💡💡 Top Tips 💡💡 {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}

* **Add comments to your code** 
  - Use a `#` at the beginning of a line or at the end of the line 
* **Avoid dots and spaces in variable names** 
  - Instead use capital letters or underscore
* **Always load packages at the start**
* **Make sure everything is spelled correctly!**
  - And capitalisation is consistent when loading in data 
* **Check Cheatsheets, especially when using a new package** 
  - Top menu Help > Cheatsheets or https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/ 
  
:::

## 💡💡 Top Tips 💡💡 {transition="none" .smaller}

::: {.incremental}

* **If you are unsure of what something does, type into the console a question mark followed by the function or package**
  - `?function` 
  - for common functions, check the [introverse package help files](https://sjspielman.github.io/introverse/articles/introverse_online.html) 
  - reading documentation is a skill that takes time to develop
* General introduction to R as a programming language: [**A Succinct Introduction to R**](https://r-guide.steveharoz.com/index.html)
* **Practice makes perfect. Build familiarity with the system and don’t be afraid to make mistakes**
* When it doubt, **Google it!** 

:::

## How to search for help effectively online?

* When in doubt, copy and paste the error into Google 
  - Include the package name or “in R” in your search. If using GenAI tools, make it explicit “in the tidyverse” 
* Built-in R help function `?function` 
* [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/r) 
* [Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co) 
* Be willing and ready to adapt code to your context 
* See document with more details
